Yes: several papers describe hierarchical or tree-based retrieval that can connect search terms to documents through summaries or chunk structure. The closest match is DTCRS, which dynamically generates summary trees, uses sub-question embeddings as initial cluster centers, and improves relevance between summaries and the question while reducing redundant nodes [2]. NavTree and SVD-RAG also use tree-structured retrieval over chunks; NavTree navigates a deterministic tree over chunks without LLM summaries, while SVD-RAG builds an extractive tree-organized retriever from dense embeddings [1, 9].

If you want an approach specifically for finding relevant text chunks through a hierarchy of summaries, the papers differ mainly in how the hierarchy is built: recursive summary trees [2], navigation over leaf chunks with no summaries [1], or extractive tree construction from embeddings [9].
